claims.text: Progress: document the patient's progress, response to and changes in treatment, and any revision of the diagnosis.
claims.quote: You should document the patient's progress, response to and changes in treatment, and revision of diagnosis

claims.text: Interval history: subsequent hospital care and follow-up inpatient consults take only an interval history, so PFSH doesn't need to be recorded.
claims.quote: For certain categories of E/M services that include only an interval history, it is not necessary to record information about the PFSH. Those categories are subsequent hospital care, follow-up inpatient consultations and subsequent nursing facility care.

claims.text: Earlier ROS/PFSH: need not be rewritten if you reviewed and updated it: describe what's new (or note no change) and give the date and location of the earlier ROS/PFSH.
claims.quote: DG: A ROS and/or a PFSH obtained during an earlier encounter does not need to be re-recorded if there is evidence that the physician reviewed and updated the previous information. This may occur when a physician updates his/her own record or in an institutional setting or group practice where many physicians use a common record. The review and update may be documented by: describing any new ROS and/or PFSH information or noting there has been no change in the information; and noting the date and location of the earlier ROS and/or PFSH.

claims.text: Why tests were ordered: if you don't write the rationale for ordering diagnostic and other ancillary services, it should be easy to infer.
claims.quote: If not documented, the rationale for ordering diagnostic and other ancillary services should be easily inferred.
claims.locator: General principles of medical record documentation, item 3

claims.text: Diagnoses on hand: past and present diagnoses should be accessible to the treating and consulting clinicians.
claims.quote: Past and present diagnoses should be accessible to the treating and/or consulting physician.
claims.locator: General principles of medical record documentation, item 4
